title: The job board
scenario:
It is Tuesday, 15:10. Your studio is making a teaser from nine shots. Eight shots run on Runway. One shot runs on Google's Veo 3.1. A caption draft runs as an OpenAI background job. The producer wants to cut the video tonight.

The job board is in the exhibit. It is made up for this case. The status names are the ones in Runway's docs. Use the vendors' docs to read it.
exhibit:
Job board, Tuesday 15:10 (made up for this case)

  Runway jobs
  shot-1   SUCCEEDED
  shot-2   SUCCEEDED
  shot-3   RUNNING      (submitted 4 minutes ago)
  shot-4   THROTTLED
  shot-5   THROTTLED
  shot-6   FAILED       (failure and failureCode are filled in)
  shot-7   CANCELLED
  shot-8   PENDING

  Veo 3.1 job
  shot-9   operation done = false   (submitted 4 minutes ago)

Notification inbox (made up for this case)
  "Caption job finished"   webhook-id: wh_0042
  "Caption job finished"   webhook-id: wh_0042

questions.prompt: Which shots have a video you can download right now?

options.text: shot-1, shot-2 and shot-3
options.explanation: shot-3 is RUNNING. A running job has nothing to download yet.

options.text: shot-1, shot-2 and shot-6
options.explanation: shot-6 is FAILED. A failed job carries failure and failureCode, not a video.

options.text: Every shot except shot-8
options.explanation: Only SUCCEEDED jobs carry output. CANCELLED, THROTTLED and RUNNING jobs do not.

options.text: shot-1 and shot-2 only
options.explanation: Right. Runway's primer says only SUCCEEDED carries an output. FAILED carries failure details. RUNNING, PENDING and THROTTLED have no output yet.

questions.prompt: A teammate wants to cancel and resubmit shot-4 and shot-5, because they are THROTTLED. What is the best move?

options.text: Delete both and ask for a different video model.
options.explanation: Nothing says the model is the problem. The jobs are waiting for capacity under your limit.

options.text: Leave them. THROTTLED is not an error. The jobs are queued behind your rate limit and will proceed on their own.
options.explanation: Right. This is how Runway's primer describes THROTTLED.

options.text: Treat them as FAILED and tell the client two shots are lost.
options.explanation: They are not failed. Runway says they will proceed on their own.

options.text: Cancel and resubmit now. THROTTLED means the job failed.
options.explanation: Runway says THROTTLED is not an error. A resubmitted job would only queue again.

questions.prompt: Shot-9 is a Veo 3.1 job, submitted 4 minutes ago. It still shows done = false. What does that tell you?

options.text: You must submit it again to make it finish faster.
options.explanation: A new request starts another job. It does not speed up the one that is running.

options.text: The job failed. A job that takes over a minute has failed.
options.explanation: Google lists a maximum latency of 6 minutes at peak hours. 4 minutes is inside that range.

options.text: Normal so far. Google says Veo latency can reach 6 minutes at peak hours. Keep checking.
options.explanation: Right. Google's limits list a latency from 11 seconds to 6 minutes at peak hours, and the job is polled until done is true.

options.text: The video is ready but hidden until you refresh the page.
options.explanation: done = false means the job is not finished. Nothing in the docs says the video is waiting.

questions.prompt: The studio will run 200 clips overnight. Which setup is best, if the tool supports it?

options.text: Poll as fast as possible all night, so you never miss a result.
options.explanation: Runway's primer says to poll with backoff rather than a tight loop.

options.text: Ask the tool to notify you when jobs finish, for example with a webhook, instead of watching a screen.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI describes webhooks as notifications to an endpoint you control, for example when a batch completes. Being told is calmer than watching for a whole night.

options.text: Refresh the job page by hand every few minutes.
options.explanation: This is possible but it does not scale to 200 jobs, and it is easy to miss a failure.

options.text: Cancel each job and run them again in the morning.
options.explanation: Cancelling throws away work for no reason. Jobs can run overnight.

questions.prompt: The inbox shows the same OpenAI "finished" notice twice, with the same webhook-id. Was the caption job run twice?

options.text: Yes, and you will be billed twice for the job.
options.explanation: Nothing in the docs links a duplicate notice to a second run or a second charge.

options.text: No. A webhook never sends the same event twice.
options.explanation: OpenAI says in rare cases it may deliver duplicates.

options.text: Yes. Two notices always mean two runs.
options.explanation: OpenAI's docs say duplicate copies of the same event can be delivered.

options.text: Not necessarily. OpenAI says it may deliver duplicate copies of an event. The same webhook-id marks it as a duplicate.
options.explanation: Right. OpenAI says the webhook-id header can be used as an idempotency key to remove duplicates.
